government.title: The Determinants of Voter Turnout in Croatian Local Government Elections
government.short_title: The Determinants of Voter Turnout in Croatian Local Government Elections
government.source: Journal of Public and Nonprofit Affairs
government.plain_summary: This study looked at why people vote in local government elections in Croatia from 2014 to 2021. It found that if fewer people voted last time, they're likely to vote less again. Issues like whether the city provides good services and benefits also affect how many people show up to vote. The main parties aren't doing a good job of getting their supporters to participate.

government.title: Did populist governance change corruption risks during crises across European countries?

government.title: Blame Avoidance and Corruption: How Politicians' Denials Shape Citizen Perceptions and Political Accountability
government.short_title: Blame Avoidance and Corruption: How Politicians' Denials Shape Citizen Perceptions and Politic…
government.plain_summary: This study examines how politicians accused of corruption respond when they deny their wrongdoing. The research shows that when politicians say they are innocent or blame others for their actions, it can improve their image and chances of winning elections. This is especially true for people who strongly support one political party. Understanding this helps us see how leaders influence public opinion about corruption in politics.

government.title: Customer Experiences with Airline Refunds: An Analysis of Procedures, Challenges, and Policy Implications
government.short_title: Customer Experiences with Airline Refunds: An Analysis of Procedures, Challenges, and Policy I…
government.source: International Journal of Research in Entrepreneurship & Business Studies
government.plain_summary: This study analyzed how airlines handle airfare refunds and the challenges customers face during this process. It found that communication issues are a major problem, especially in understanding airline rules. Despite most customers being satisfied with their refund after receiving one, they felt the process was complex and inefficient. The research suggests clearer policies and better coordination between airlines, intermediaries, and customers could improve trust and service quality.

government.title: Strengthening Coastal Resilience through Science-Based Mangrove Governance in Davao Occidental, Philippines
government.short_title: Strengthening Coastal Resilience through Science-Based Mangrove Governance in Davao Occidental…
government.plain_summary: This research highlights that while investing in mangrove restoration in Davao Occidental has been significant, outcomes have varied widely due to issues like incorrect species selection and lack of monitoring. Studies show that by matching the right species to each site and diversifying plant types, survival rates can be very high at over 95%. However, these effective methods are not consistently used because there's no unified policy framework. The study suggests creating a standardized governance system that mandates correct species use, promotes diverse planting strategies, and establishes community monitoring systems supported by partnerships between local governments and universities.

government.title: Decoding Moral Vulnerability in AI Environments:A Case Study of Algorithmic Governance and Policy Implications
government.short_title: Decoding Moral Vulnerability in AI Environments:A Case Study of Algorithmic Governance and Pol…
government.plain_summary: This study examines how using AI in professional environments can lead to a situation called "moral vulnerability." This happens when AI systems are used without proper ethical guidelines, which can make people feel uncomfortable or undervalued. The research found that this can cause issues like reduced sense of responsibility and instability in one's role within the organization. To prevent these problems, it suggests several practical steps for leaders to take, such as conducting assessments before using new AI systems, adding some extra steps in user interfaces to slow down decision-making processes, and having independent groups review digital ethics. These suggestions are meant to help protect organizations from potential harm caused by poorly managed AI use.

government.title: The Impact of Digital Technology on International Humanitarian Law: Ethical and Legal Implications of Autonomous Weapons Systems
government.short_title: The Impact of Digital Technology on International Humanitarian Law: Ethical and Legal Implicat…
government.source: European Journal of Law and Political Science
government.plain_summary: This article looks at how new technology like AI is changing international laws for wars. As weapons get more automated, it raises questions about who should be held responsible when they make decisions. The main idea is that current rules are still useful but need updating to fit with these new types of weapons. It suggests ways to improve the existing laws so that people in war zones can continue to rely on protections like not harming civilians unnecessarily.

government.title: International Anti-Corruption Commissions: Explaining Institutional Design and Autonomy
government.short_title: International Anti-Corruption Commissions: Explaining Institutional Design and Autonomy
government.plain_summary: Political corruption is a big problem that governments often struggle with and sometimes use anti-corruption measures against their own democracy. International Anti-Corruption Commissions (IACCs) help address this issue by working with both international experts and local people. Some IACCs have more independence than others, which can affect how effective they are in fighting corruption. In places like northern Central America, when there are coalitions that include government insiders and activists at the table during negotiations, these groups use their influence to make sure anti-corruption efforts don't undermine democracy too much.

government.title: The Transparency Paradox: How Digital Accountability Can Inflate Public Costs in Low-Trust Environments
government.short_title: The Transparency Paradox: How Digital Accountability Can Inflate Public Costs in Low-Trust Env…

government.title: Governance, Democracy & Psychological Wellbeing Psychology of a Corruption
government.short_title: Governance, Democracy & Psychological Wellbeing Psychology of a Corruption
government.source: Journal of Business and Econometrics Studies
government.plain_summary: This paper looks at corruption in Africa by examining how it affects governance, democracy, and mental health. It suggests that corruption is not just a legal issue but also stems from deep social and moral problems left over from colonial times. The study proposes solutions like strengthening institutions, developing ethical leaders, empowering citizens, and using restorative justice methods. By doing this, they aim to improve people's well-being and strengthen democratic systems in Africa.

government.title: Artificial Intelligence Adoption in Public Administration: Challenges for Accountability, Transparency, and Public Service Delivery
government.short_title: Artificial Intelligence Adoption in Public Administration: Challenges for Accountability, Tran…
government.plain_summary: This research looks at how artificial intelligence is being used in government services. It found that while AI can speed up service delivery and improve monitoring of processes, it also creates issues like unclear responsibility for decisions made by AI systems, lack of transparency about these decisions, uneven readiness among staff to use AI, and risks to human decision-making. To address these challenges, the study recommends creating clear guidelines on accountability, making AI explanations transparent, encouraging public disclosure, ensuring human oversight over AI processes, providing training for staff, and offering ways for citizens to appeal if they have concerns about AI decisions.

government.title: International Anti-Corruption Models and Mechanisms
government.short_title: International Anti-Corruption Models and Mechanisms
government.plain_summary: This study from Georgian Technical University talks about how corruption is a big problem in modern societies. It affects everything from politics to economy and can make people lose trust in their government. Because of this, it's important for countries to have ways to stop corruption like laws and programs that punish those who do wrong things. By doing so, they can keep the system fairer and more stable for everyone.

government.title: AI Regulation and Its Social Impacts on Public Policy
government.short_title: AI Regulation and Its Social Impacts on Public Policy
government.plain_summary: AI is now a key part of how governments make decisions in many areas like healthcare, policing, and welfare. As more AI systems are used, it's important to have rules to make sure they work fairly and don't cause problems. These rules help ensure that AI doesn't lead to unfair treatment or less democracy. By carefully watching how AI is used, we can make sure it helps people and doesn't hurt them.

government.title: The dark side of public service motivation : Analysis of noble cause corruption based on the Lebanese case
government.short_title: The dark side of public service motivation : Analysis of noble cause corruption based on the L…
government.plain_summary: This study examines how public service motivation can lead to noble cause corruption in Lebanon, where there's a lot of social and economic hardship. The research found that feelings like compassion and selflessness often push people into doing good deeds for noble causes, but these actions sometimes involve corrupt practices. This leads to internal conflicts as the person feels both guilty and supported by their work environment. Factors like physical exchanges, personal space in the workplace, and close relationships with users can make it easier for this type of corruption to happen.

government.title: La face sombre de la motivation de service public : Analyse de la corruption pour une cause noble à partir du cas libanais
government.short_title: La face sombre de la motivation de service public : Analyse de la corruption pour une cause no…
government.plain_summary: This study examines how public service motivation can lead to corruption for a noble cause in Lebanon, where corruption is prevalent and social issues are challenging. Based on interviews with 32 Lebanese public servants, the research explores how feelings of compassion and self-sacrifice related to public service motivation might encourage them to engage in corrupt behavior for what they see as a good cause. The study highlights that these motivations can lead to behaviors like providing extra support or shielding users from punishment. This can create internal conflicts within the public servant due to their emotional connection with those affected.

government.title: Simultaneous Model Discovery and State Estimation under High Data Corruption
government.short_title: Simultaneous Model Discovery and State Estimation under High Data Corruption

government.title: Innovation entry as governance filter: shaping exploratory digital innovation in the public sector
government.short_title: Innovation entry as governance filter: shaping exploratory digital innovation in the public se…
government.source: Transforming Government: People, Process and Policy
government.plain_summary: This study looks at how the way government organizations handle new ideas affects their ability to try out innovative technologies and approaches. Many public sector groups are used to solving problems step-by-step, but this can make it hard to explore new ideas freely. The research found that the rules for starting and moving through innovation projects act like filters, often pushing exploratory work towards more traditional ways of working. This means they tend to focus on quick fixes rather than experimenting with different solutions.

government.title: Factors Influencing Political Stability in South America: The Roles of Rule of Law, Regulatory Quality, Control of Corruption, and Government Effectiveness
government.short_title: Factors Influencing Political Stability in South America: The Roles of Rule of Law, Regulatory…
government.source: Greenation International Journal of Law and Social Sciences
government.plain_summary: Political stability in South American countries varies greatly and is influenced by several factors including rule of law, regulatory quality, control of corruption, and government effectiveness. This research found that all these governance aspects contribute positively to stability but only the rule of law has a significant impact when considered together with other variables. The study suggests that strengthening legal systems and improving law enforcement could be crucial for maintaining long-term political stability in South America.

government.title: Enhancing Police and Judicial Accountability in Gender-Based Violence Cases: Addressing Corruption, Inefficiency, and Victim-Blaming in Law Enforcement and the Judiciary
government.short_title: Enhancing Police and Judicial Accountability in Gender-Based Violence Cases: Addressing Corrup…
government.source: OIDA International Journal of Sustainable Development
government.plain_summary: This research highlights significant issues within law enforcement and the judiciary regarding gender-based violence (GBV) cases in South Africa. Key problems include corruption, inefficiency, and a tendency to blame victims instead of perpetrators. To address these challenges, it suggests strengthening anti-corruption measures, providing specialized training for officers and judges, and adopting survivor-centered justice approaches. These changes are crucial for improving accountability and ensuring fair treatment for GBV survivors while upholding the rule of law.

government.title: SHADOW ECONOMY AND CORRUPTION RISKS IN THE SYSTEM OF THREATS TO THE ECONOMIC SECURITY OF THE REGION
government.short_title: SHADOW ECONOMY AND CORRUPTION RISKS IN THE SYSTEM OF THREATS TO THE ECONOMIC SECURITY OF THE R…
government.source: ECONOMIC BULLETIN OF THE DNIPROVSK STATE TECHNICAL UNIVERSITY
government.plain_summary: This article discusses how the shadow economy and corruption affect the economic security of a region. It shows that the shadow economy can weaken financial stability, reduce tax revenues, and distort competition. Corruption in areas like public procurement and land administration creates opportunities for illegal activities. This leads to inefficiencies in governance, reduces trust in government, and harms investment climates.

government.title: ЗАРУБЕЖНЫЙ ОПЫТ БОРЬБЫ С КОРРУПЦИЕЙ И ПОВЫШЕНИЯ АНТИКОРРУПЦИОННОГО ПРАВОСОЗНАНИЯ ГРАЖДАН
government.short_title: ЗАРУБЕЖНЫЙ ОПЫТ БОРЬБЫ С КОРРУПЦИЕЙ И ПОВЫШЕНИЯ АНТИКОРРУПЦИОННОГО ПРАВОСОЗНАНИЯ ГРАЖДАН
government.plain_summary: This article looks at how other countries handle corruption and ways to improve anti-corruption efforts. It discusses different models like centralized control in places like Singapore and decentralized systems in the USA. The study covers things like educating people about corruption, making government information public, using technology for transparency, offering incentives to officials, and having a system where citizens can report corrupt behavior. The main point is that effectiveness isn't just about centralizing or decentralizing power; it's also important how well these three parts work together: laws, institutions, and educating people.

government.title: E-Government to Combat Corruption Worldwide: Dominant Factors and a Holistic Model Emerging From Structured Literature Review
government.short_title: E-Government to Combat Corruption Worldwide: Dominant Factors and a Holistic Model Emerging Fr…
government.source: Journal of Global Information Technology Management

government.title: Corruption, collective moral harm, and the limits of the non-prosecution agreement as a reparatory mechanism for vulnerable groups
government.short_title: Corruption, collective moral harm, and the limits of the non-prosecution agreement as a repara…
government.plain_summary: This study examines whether a non-prosecution agreement (NPA) is enough to address corruption's impact on vulnerable groups. The NPA is seen as a way to resolve disputes without going to court but assumes that it can fully compensate for the harm caused by corruption, which affects more than just public funds and official misconduct. However, the study finds this approach insufficient because it doesn't adequately protect communities affected by corruption from moral damage. It argues that while NPA helps in some cases, it lacks provisions specifically designed to address collective harm like deepening inequalities or damaging a community's dignity.

government.title: Anti‐Corruption and Luxury Goods Consumption: Evidence From the Chinese Cigarette Market
government.short_title: Anti‐Corruption and Luxury Goods Consumption: Evidence From the Chinese Cigarette Market
government.source: Oxford Bulletin of Economics and Statistics
government.plain_summary: This study examines how anti-corruption measures affect luxury goods consumption, focusing on the cigarette market in China. The researchers developed a theory suggesting that corruption influences people's willingness to buy expensive items like cigarettes. They used data from 2007 to 2014 to see if China’s anti-corruption campaign had an impact. Their findings showed that while the overall sales of cigarettes increased, luxury brands saw less demand compared to cheaper ones.

government.title: Determinants of corruption control in public sectors in Northwestern Ethiopia
government.short_title: Determinants of corruption control in public sectors in Northwestern Ethiopia
government.plain_summary: This research examines what helps or hinders efforts to stop corruption in public sector organizations in Northwestern Ethiopia. It found that having strong rules (institutional factors), cultural norms against bribery, fair political systems, ethical guidelines, and people who follow the rules are important for reducing corruption. Economic factors didn't have a big impact. To improve these controls, it suggests strengthening existing laws, making sure anti-corruption bodies operate independently, increasing access to information, educating people about ethics, and providing regular training for leaders in public offices.

government.title: How ethical leadership reduces corruption in Pakistan’s public sector: job satisfaction as a mediator
government.short_title: How ethical leadership reduces corruption in Pakistan’s public sector: job satisfaction as a m…
government.plain_summary: This research looks at how ethical leadership can reduce corruption among public employees in Pakistan. It found that when leaders are ethical, it leads to higher job satisfaction for their staff. Higher job satisfaction then reduces the likelihood of corruption by making workers feel more committed to serving the public. This study suggests that if managers promote ethical behavior and boost employee happiness, they can help prevent corrupt practices in government.

government.title: Ethical and Legal Implications of AI-Driven Anti-Corruption Technologies in Developing Democracies
government.short_title: Ethical and Legal Implications of AI-Driven Anti-Corruption Technologies in Developing Democra…
government.source: African Journal of Law Political Research and Administration
government.plain_summary: This study looks at how AI can help spot fraud in government spending in countries that are just starting to have democratic systems. It suggests that using AI like machine learning could make it easier for people to see if money is being spent unfairly or wasted. However, there are still big challenges like not having enough good data or fair rules. The main idea is that while AI can be useful, it needs to work with human checks and balances to really help stop corruption.

government.title: Corruption and the Composition of Business Activity in Brazil
government.short_title: Corruption and the Composition of Business Activity in Brazil
government.plain_summary: Corruption affects how businesses are distributed across different industries. In Brazil, areas with higher levels of corruption tend to have fewer jobs and business establishments in sectors like construction and manufacturing. Instead, there's a larger presence of agricultural activities. The study also found that where corruption is more prevalent, the competition among businesses becomes tighter or less competitive depending on the sector.

government.title: PENTAHELIX MODEL COLLABORATION AS A COLLECTIVE EFFORT IN ANTI-CORRUPTION ECOSYSTEMS
government.short_title: PENTAHELIX MODEL COLLABORATION AS A COLLECTIVE EFFORT IN ANTI-CORRUPTION ECOSYSTEMS
government.source: Journal of Social Politics and Governance (JSPG)
government.plain_summary: This study looks at how different groups like governments, businesses, non-profits, schools, and media work together to fight corruption using something called the Pentahelix framework. It found that for effective anti-corruption efforts, these groups need to collaborate closely rather than working separately. The Pentahelix model shows they can tackle corruption more effectively when they all play a part in it. This collaborative approach is key to creating strong systems against corruption and making sure it doesn't happen anymore.

government.title: Building Village Financial Accountability through Transparency: The Role of Serial Mediators in Commitment and Integrity of Village Government Apparatus in South Sumatra Province
government.short_title: Building Village Financial Accountability through Transparency: The Role of Serial Mediators i…
government.source: Dinasti International Journal of Education Management and Social Science
government.plain_summary: This study examines how transparency affects financial accountability in villages in South Sumatra Province by looking at the roles of commitment and integrity among local government officials. It found that when villagers are more transparent about their finances, it leads to higher levels of commitment and integrity from officials. This, in turn, improves financial accountability within the village. However, there's no direct effect of transparency on financial accountability itself.

government.title: Regulating Artificial Intelligence in the Public Sector: Policy Frameworks for Accountability, Ethics, and Human Rights Protection
government.short_title: Regulating Artificial Intelligence in the Public Sector: Policy Frameworks for Accountability,…
government.plain_summary: This research examines how governments can manage artificial intelligence effectively while ensuring they're accountable for its decisions, follow ethical guidelines, and protect people's rights. It found that transparency, having someone supervise AI systems, and regular audits are important ways to hold AI accountable. Ethical principles like fairness and avoiding discrimination need to be followed more consistently than what policies promise. To keep privacy safe and ensure everyone has a say in how AI is used, it’s crucial for governments to have independent oversight bodies.

government.title: Digital Governance and Anti-Corruption Transformation in Algeria: Evaluating the Role of Fiscal Digitization and E-Procurement Systems in Enhancing Administrative Transparency and Public Sector Integrity
government.short_title: Digital Governance and Anti-Corruption Transformation in Algeria: Evaluating the Role of Fisca…
government.source: Science, Education and Innovations in the context of modern problems
government.plain_summary: Digital governance in Algeria has been adopted as a strategy to combat corruption, especially in sectors like taxation and procurement. The country is digitizing tax administration and implementing electronic public procurement systems, which have improved transparency and accountability. These digital tools help reduce discretionary practices, enhance traceability, and improve access to information for the public. However, there are still challenges such as incomplete integration of digital systems, cybersecurity issues, and uneven administrative capacity that need addressing.

government.title: Effectiveness of School-Based Anti-Drug Clubs in Raising Awareness of the Dangers of Drug Abuse Among Students in Basic Education Schools in Abuja Municipal Area Council, Nigeria
government.short_title: Effectiveness of School-Based Anti-Drug Clubs in Raising Awareness of the Dangers of Drug Abus…
government.source: Journal of Education Research and Library Practice
government.plain_summary: This research looked at how well anti-drug clubs work in schools to teach students about the dangers of using drugs. In Abuja, Nigeria, they surveyed 300 middle school students who were part of these clubs. The study found that these clubs are very effective in helping students understand why drug use is bad for their health and future. Students agreed that club activities helped them learn more about how drugs can affect their grades, friendships, laws, and mental health.

government.title: Correction: Reforming the white coat economy: judicial evidence and institutional implications from China's healthcare anti-corruption campaign
government.short_title: Correction: Reforming the white coat economy: judicial evidence and institutional implications…

government.title: Exploring the Anti-Inflammatory Potential of Choerospondias axillaris Through Molecular Docking based in silico Pharmacological Investigation
government.short_title: Exploring the Anti-Inflammatory Potential of Choerospondias axillaris Through Molecular Dockin…
government.source: Journal of Manmohan Memorial Institute of Health Sciences
government.plain_summary: This study compared hormone and bone health indicators between women before and after menopause. It found that postmenopausal women had higher thyroid-stimulating hormone (TSH) levels and alkaline phosphatase (ALP), along with lower calcium and phosphate in their blood. The research used various statistical methods to analyze these markers, including multivariate analysis and machine learning models like random forest which showed 81% accuracy in predicting menopausal status based on ALP and calcium levels. Age also influenced calcium levels more than menopause status did.

government.title: Anti-Corruption Compliance Abroad: Best Practices
government.short_title: Anti-Corruption Compliance Abroad: Best Practices
government.source: Public International and Private International Law
government.plain_summary: This article looks at how different countries handle preventing corruption both in their own laws and internationally. It shows that now companies need to prove they have effective anti-corruption programs rather than just having them. The study found many small businesses in Russia are vulnerable to corruption, which isn't enough protection yet. Countries like Brazil, UK, Portugal, US, and France all agree on the basics of how to do this well, but their rules vary a lot.

government.title: Unpacking the Emergence of Unqualified Audit Opinions as Quasi‐Accountability in Indonesian Public Sector
government.short_title: Unpacking the Emergence of Unqualified Audit Opinions as Quasi‐Accountability in Indonesian Pu…
government.plain_summary: This research looks at how unqualified audit opinions (UAOs) are used in Indonesian local governments. Despite an increase in these opinions, they don't necessarily mean stronger accountability. Instead, their rise shows that audits support claims about government integrity and fighting corruption. Auditors play a key role here, balancing expectations from the environment with their own risks.

government.title: Political power and wealth distribution: how anti-corruption reforms reshape inequality
government.short_title: Political power and wealth distribution: how anti-corruption reforms reshape inequality
government.plain_summary: This study looks at how anti-corruption measures affect who gets rich from government actions. By using data from many countries, it found that when governments take steps to reduce corruption over time, the top earners don't get as much wealth anymore. At the same time, people at the bottom of the income ladder see a small increase in their share of total wealth. These changes happen gradually and last for years.

government.short_title: Local Government Transparency and Citizen Satisfaction: Examining the Role of Public Trust and…

government.short_title: Do Majority Shifts Reduce Corruption in Korean Local Council?

government.short_title: Corrigendum: Editorial: Governance and accountability (Gover-nability) of multiple values of m…

government.short_title: Faith, Fraud, and Fees: Is Vigilant Behavior of Religious Donors in Crowdfunding Sacred or Sec…

government.title: A Study on the Use of Blockchain Technology to Prevent and Detect Corruption in Thailand's Government Procurement Process
government.short_title: A Study on the Use of Blockchain Technology to Prevent and Detect Corruption in Thailand's Gov…
government.source: International Journal of Electronic Government Research
government.plain_summary: This research suggests using blockchain technology to help stop corruption in government buying things. It found that having a good understanding of how to use blockchain is still not common among Thai governments. The study recommends creating new systems with blockchain like smart contracts and online training programs to make sure everyone follows rules fairly during the buying process. This can improve trust between buyers, sellers, and officials.

government.title: Governing Algorithmic Fairness in Climate-Health Systems: A Policy Framework for Bias Mitigation in Public Sector Decision-Making
government.short_title: Governing Algorithmic Fairness in Climate-Health Systems: A Policy Framework for Bias Mitigati…
government.source: Journal of Public Policy and Local Government (JPPLG)
government.plain_summary: This article discusses how artificial intelligence is being used to help make decisions about climate and health issues in government. While this technology can be very useful, it also has the potential to unfairly treat certain groups of people if not managed properly. The paper introduces a new framework called AFCHG that helps governments use AI fairly when making these kinds of decisions. This framework includes four main parts: setting rules, ensuring fair decision-making processes, fixing any unfairness in how AI works, and considering fairness for all people.

government.title: ETHICS AND LEGAL FRAMEWORK OF PUBLIC RELATIONS VISUAL COMMUNICATION AS A MEDIA OF PUBLIC EDUCATION IN ENCOURAGING SUSTAINABLE GLOBAL ECONOMIC RECOVERY IN THE ERA OF DIGITAL TRANSFORMATION
government.short_title: ETHICS AND LEGAL FRAMEWORK OF PUBLIC RELATIONS VISUAL COMMUNICATION AS A MEDIA OF PUBLIC EDUCA…
government.source: International Journal of Law Government and Communication
government.plain_summary: Digital transformations have made using visuals an important part of how Public Relations communicates information. This helps educate people about things like sustainable economic recovery. But with more use of digital visuals comes new rules and ethical standards to follow. Our research looked at these issues, finding that following good ethics and staying within legal guidelines is key for effective PR communication.

government.title: Governing Money Laundering as a Collective-Action Problem: The European Anti-Money Laundering Authority (AMLA)
government.short_title: Governing Money Laundering as a Collective-Action Problem: The European Anti-Money Laundering…
government.plain_summary: Money laundering is a significant threat affecting competitive markets, security, and consumer well-being. The European Anti-Money Laundering Authority (AMLA) was created as part of new EU regulations to improve supervisory standards and coordinate the fight against illicit finance across Europe. AMLA combines classification functions like setting rules and standards with selective enforcement tools such as direct supervision of high-risk groups and escalation mechanisms. By viewing these aspects through a collective-action lens, it helps explain how AMLA can effectively police money laundering while also highlighting its limitations in fully addressing the issue.

government.title: Development of Anti-Corruption Declaration in Russia: Legal Aspects and Contemporary Challenges
government.short_title: Development of Anti-Corruption Declaration in Russia: Legal Aspects and Contemporary Challenges
government.plain_summary: This article looks at how Russia is making rules for people to declare if they have done anything wrong that could be seen as corrupt. In recent years, it's gotten more complicated how this works. On one hand, there are now better ways for government to check on people who might be doing bad things and use computers more. But on the other hand, fewer people can easily see these declarations because the government says they need to protect everyone from danger.

government.title: Relevant Issues of Conducting Anti-Corruption Expert Examination of Draft Regulatory Legal Acts by State Authorities of the Subjects of the Russian Federation
government.short_title: Relevant Issues of Conducting Anti-Corruption Expert Examination of Draft Regulatory Legal Act…
government.plain_summary: This article talks about how state authorities in different parts of Russia can check if new rules they're making are free from corruption. It looks at ways to do this effectively and gives examples from other regions. The main idea is to suggest improvements so these checks work better, helping keep laws clean and fair for everyone.

government.title: Implementation of Good Governance Principles in the 2024 Election: A Study of Transparency and Accountability in the Central Maluku Regency KPU
government.short_title: Implementation of Good Governance Principles in the 2024 Election: A Study of Transparency and…
government.plain_summary: This study examines how transparently and accountable the 2024 election in Central Maluku Regency was. It found that while there was good openness of information to the public about voting processes, including updates on voter data and results announcements, improvements are needed in technical aspects like reporting and documentation consistency. Additionally, better coordination between election organizers and oversight bodies is required for smoother operations. Practitioners can use these findings to improve future elections by enhancing transparency, accountability, and coordination among different stakeholders.

government.title: Evaluating the effectiveness of the implementation of the regional financial management information system in public sector institutions
government.short_title: Evaluating the effectiveness of the implementation of the regional financial management inform…
government.source: Strengthening Dynamic System: e-Government and Public Services
government.plain_summary: This research evaluates how the Regional Financial Management Information System (SIPKD) works in public sector institutions. It found that SIPKD improved data integration and report accuracy, making it easier for officials to monitor finances in real-time. Users appreciated its accessibility and usefulness for daily tasks. However, challenges like human error, network issues, and insufficient staff skills still need addressing.

government.title: Navigating the public sector: a quantitative investigation of organisational factors influencing ERP implementation in New Zealand
government.short_title: Navigating the public sector: a quantitative investigation of organisational factors influenci…
government.source: Transforming Government: People, Process and Policy
government.plain_summary: This study investigates how certain organizational factors impact the successful implementation of Enterprise Resource Planning (ERP) systems in New Zealand's government agencies. It found that leadership commitment, organizational preparedness, user capability development, and change management readiness are crucial for ERP success. Leadership support was identified as the strongest predictor of ERP deployment success. Interestingly, cultural differences did not significantly affect ERP outcomes.

government.title: The Challenges of Implementing E-government in the Public Sector: A Case Study on The Gambia
government.short_title: The Challenges of Implementing E-government in the Public Sector: A Case Study on The Gambia
government.plain_summary: E-government has become a way for governments to deliver services more efficiently and make governance transparent. However, implementing it can be challenging, especially in developing countries with limited resources. A case study from The Gambia found that while e-government helps improve service delivery, transparency, accountability, and citizen participation, there are still big hurdles like not having enough IT infrastructure or skilled employees to use digital tools effectively. There's also a lack of collaboration between different government departments and issues related to internet access and trust in government services.

government.short_title: Beyond Compliance: A Systematic Review of Ethics, Accountability, And Transparency in Indonesi…
government.plain_summary: This study looks at how ethics, accountability, and transparency work together in Indonesian government systems. It found that even with digitalization efforts, if there isn't a strong enough foundation of ethics, these measures can fail to prevent corruption and lose public trust. The research suggests integrating ethical practices, making information transparent, and ensuring accountability are all important for effective governance. By combining these elements, Indonesia can improve its government systems and build more trustworthy relationships with the people it serves.

government.short_title: CHALLENGES AND DIRECTIONS FOR IMPROVING THE EFFECTIVENESS OF UKRAINE’S STATE ANTI-CORRUPTION B…
government.plain_summary: This article discusses key issues facing Ukraine's anti-corruption bodies and suggests ways to improve their effectiveness. Challenges include fragmented legal support, political instability, lack of coordination among agencies, limited resources, unclear jurisdictional powers, and low public trust. To address these, the Ukrainian government should focus on strengthening institutional independence, optimizing power distribution, improving human resources, enhancing coordination mechanisms, and increasing transparency in sensitive areas like procurement and financial controls. These steps are crucial for building trust with society and aligning anti-corruption efforts with European standards of governance.

nonprofit.title: The Determinants of Voter Turnout in Croatian Local Government Elections
nonprofit.short_title: The Determinants of Voter Turnout in Croatian Local Government Elections
nonprofit.source: Journal of Public and Nonprofit Affairs
nonprofit.plain_summary: This study looked at why people vote in local government elections in Croatia from 2014 to 2021. It found that if fewer people voted last time, they're likely to vote less again. Issues like whether the city provides good services and benefits also affect how many people show up to vote. The main parties aren't doing a good job of getting their supporters to participate.

nonprofit.source: International Journal of Research in Entrepreneurship & Business Studies
nonprofit.plain_summary: This study analyzed how airlines handle airfare refunds and the challenges customers face during this process. It found that communication issues are a major problem, especially in understanding airline rules. Despite most customers being satisfied with their refund after receiving one, they felt the process was complex and inefficient. The research suggests clearer policies and better coordination between airlines, intermediaries, and customers could improve trust and service quality.

nonprofit.title: Artificial Intelligence Adoption in Public Administration: Challenges for Accountability, Transparency, and Public Service Delivery
nonprofit.short_title: Artificial Intelligence Adoption in Public Administration: Challenges for Accountability, Tran…
nonprofit.plain_summary: This research looks at how artificial intelligence is being used in government services. It found that while AI can speed up service delivery and improve monitoring of processes, it also creates issues like unclear responsibility for decisions made by AI systems, lack of transparency about these decisions, uneven readiness among staff to use AI, and risks to human decision-making. To address these challenges, the study recommends creating clear guidelines on accountability, making AI explanations transparent, encouraging public disclosure, ensuring human oversight over AI processes, providing training for staff, and offering ways for citizens to appeal if they have concerns about AI decisions.

nonprofit.title: Determinants of corruption control in public sectors in Northwestern Ethiopia
nonprofit.short_title: Determinants of corruption control in public sectors in Northwestern Ethiopia
nonprofit.plain_summary: This research examines what helps or hinders efforts to stop corruption in public sector organizations in Northwestern Ethiopia. It found that having strong rules (institutional factors), cultural norms against bribery, fair political systems, ethical guidelines, and people who follow the rules are important for reducing corruption. Economic factors didn't have a big impact. To improve these controls, it suggests strengthening existing laws, making sure anti-corruption bodies operate independently, increasing access to information, educating people about ethics, and providing regular training for leaders in public offices.

nonprofit.title: PENTAHELIX MODEL COLLABORATION AS A COLLECTIVE EFFORT IN ANTI-CORRUPTION ECOSYSTEMS
nonprofit.short_title: PENTAHELIX MODEL COLLABORATION AS A COLLECTIVE EFFORT IN ANTI-CORRUPTION ECOSYSTEMS
nonprofit.source: Journal of Social Politics and Governance (JSPG)
nonprofit.plain_summary: This study looks at how different groups like governments, businesses, non-profits, schools, and media work together to fight corruption using something called the Pentahelix framework. It found that for effective anti-corruption efforts, these groups need to collaborate closely rather than working separately. The Pentahelix model shows they can tackle corruption more effectively when they all play a part in it. This collaborative approach is key to creating strong systems against corruption and making sure it doesn't happen anymore.

nonprofit.title: Regulating Artificial Intelligence in the Public Sector: Policy Frameworks for Accountability, Ethics, and Human Rights Protection
nonprofit.short_title: Regulating Artificial Intelligence in the Public Sector: Policy Frameworks for Accountability,…
nonprofit.plain_summary: This research examines how governments can manage artificial intelligence effectively while ensuring they're accountable for its decisions, follow ethical guidelines, and protect people's rights. It found that transparency, having someone supervise AI systems, and regular audits are important ways to hold AI accountable. Ethical principles like fairness and avoiding discrimination need to be followed more consistently than what policies promise. To keep privacy safe and ensure everyone has a say in how AI is used, it’s crucial for governments to have independent oversight bodies.

nonprofit.plain_summary: Digital transformations have made using visuals an important part of how Public Relations communicates information. This helps educate people about things like sustainable economic recovery. But with more use of digital visuals comes new rules and ethical standards to follow. Our research looked at these issues, finding that following good ethics and staying within legal guidelines is key for effective PR communication.
